verdict.rationale: Entra ID documents Lifecycle Workflows, which are processes that run automatically against users as they move through lifecycle phases. Conditional Access adds if-then policy rules that trigger an MFA requirement when a user tries to access an app. Both are event-driven rules, but the evidence covers only identity-lifecycle and sign-in scenarios, not general user-defined event-to-action automation. Missing for 10: documentation of configurable triggers and conditions, a catalog of available actions, custom or extensible actions beyond lifecycle and access policy, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Workflows contain specific processes that run automatically against users as they move through their lifecycle.
Lifecycle workflows (LCW) are identity governance capabilities that enable organizations to manage Microsoft Entra users across the three phases of a user's lifecycle with an organization
If a user wants to access an application or service like Microsoft 365, then they must perform multifactor authentication to gain access.
